name: Scheduled Web Scrape to Sheet with Change Detection

meta.description: Cron -> scrape a public sandbox site -> normalise -> diff against a Postgres snapshot -> append only new/changed rows -> log the run. Credentialed nodes ship disabled.

nodes.name: Fetch Page
nodes.notes: books.toscrape.com is a public sandbox built for scraping practice. Respect robots.txt and any target's terms in real work.

parameters.query: SELECT url, price, availability FROM scrape_snapshot WHERE url IN ($1) LIMIT 1000;

nodes.name: Load Previous Snapshot
nodes.notes: Disabled: needs a Postgres credential. Enable this one FIRST — the diff node reads from it, so if it is disabled the diff has no previous state and treats every row as new.

parameters.query: INSERT INTO scrape_snapshot (url, price, availability, rating, scraped_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5) ON CONFLICT (url) DO UPDATE SET price = EXCLUDED.price, availability = EXCLUDED.availability, rating = EXCLUDED.rating, scraped_at = EXCLUDED.scraped_at;

nodes.name: Upsert Snapshot
nodes.notes: Disabled: needs a Postgres credential. ON CONFLICT makes the run idempotent, so a re-run cannot duplicate rows.

parameters.content:
## Scheduled Scrape -> Sheet

**Polls every 6h, writes only what changed.**

1. `Every 6 Hours` — cron
2. `Fetch Page` — one catalogue page
3. `Parse + Normalise` — coerces every field; **throws on 0 items**
4. `Load Previous Snapshot` — Postgres
5. `Diff Against Snapshot` — new or price/availability moved
6. `Append Changes` / `Upsert Snapshot`

### Why the throw on 0 items
A selector that stops matching returns nothing. Written to a sheet,
that looks like "nothing changed this week" — which is indistinguishable from a working scraper that legitimately found no changes. Throwing makes the distinction visible.

### Why diff, not full re-append
Re-appending every 6h duplicates the sheet and burns quota for no new information. This is what makes the job cheap to leave running.

### Schema
```sql
CREATE TABLE scrape_snapshot (
  url          TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  price        NUMERIC,
  availability TEXT,
  rating       NUMERIC,
  scraped_at   TIMESTAMPTZ
);
```
